rubric.reason: PRPs/prds/text-search.prd.md:241-244 states verbatim that 'TaskFilter in src/shared/task-filter.ts gains q: string | null, keeping one filter state' — read with the shipped src/shared/task-filter.ts:20-27 (the interface member is `q: string | null;`, no `?`) and the plan's own Task 4 ACTION/Files-to-Change row, q is a REQUIRED field on TaskFilter, exactly like status/priority/from/to; tsconfig.base.json's exactOptionalPropertyTypes is inapplicable since q is not declared optional. Reproduced independently via `npx tsc -b`: exactly three errors, no others — test/task-filter.test.ts:45 (TS2741, the `const filter: TaskFilter = {...}` literal inside 'carries every set dimension in one query string, in a fixed order'), test/task-filter.test.ts:83 (TS2345, the inline object literal argument to activeCount(...) inside 'never exceeds three'), and test/task-filter.test.ts:134 (TS2741, the `const rich: TaskFilter = {...}` literal inside 'touches no dimension but its own') — all three omit q. The test pair's own diff already applied the identical EXISTING_TEST_UPDATED fix pattern to the EMPTY_FILTER deep-equality assertion (test/task-filter.test.ts, the 'EMPTY_FILTER has all five dimensions null' case, now asserting q: null), which is exactly the fix the plan's own Risk table prescribed for that one assertion — but the same session left these three other TaskFilter-typed literals in the same file unfixed. This is not merely a type-checker nicety: because q is required, filter.q on these literals is undefined at runtime, and toQuery's `if (filter.q !== null) params.set("q", filter.q)` check (undefined !== null is true) would append a spurious `q=undefined` to the exact query strings two of these tests assert do NOT contain q — so the tests' current state is wrong on both the type and the behavioral axis. The Implementer's own read-only charter (R-X, D17, no carve-out) forbids it from editing any test file regardless of how narrow or mechanical the fix is, and Validation Levels 1 (npm run check, which runs tsc -b) and 3 (npm run build) cannot pass while these three literals are stale. DISPUTE_UPHELD_TEST_WRONG: add q: null to the three cited literals — the same non-weakening EXISTING_TEST_UPDATED lifecycle fix already applied once in this same file, asserting no new behavior. Secondary note, not adjudicated as part of this dispute: the Implementer also reported the plan's own Level 2 script fails because src/shared/search.ts imports './api' extensionless; independently reproduced via `node --experimental-strip-types --input-type=module`, which throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND resolving './api'. This mirrors an existing repo convention (src/shared/format.ts also imports './dates' extensionless) and is a defect in the plan's own Validation Command, not a test-file dispute — out of scope for this arbitration channel and left for the COMMAND to route separately.

dispute_evidence.claim: The approved plan's Task 4, grounded in the PRD Architecture Notes ("TaskFilter in src/shared/task-filter.ts gains q: string | null, keeping one filter state"), makes TaskFilter.q a REQUIRED field like status/priority/from/to. The test pair updated only the EMPTY_FILTER deep-equality assertion (now line ~195) to include q: null, but three other TaskFilter-typed literals in the same file omit q (line 45 `const filter: TaskFilter = {...}`, line 83's inline activeCount({...}) argument, line 134 `const rich: TaskFilter = {...}`), so tsc -b fails with TS2741/TS2345 and Validation Levels 1 and 3 cannot pass without editing a test file, which R-X forbids the implementer.
dispute_evidence.proposed_resolution: Add q: null to those three literals — the same EXISTING_TEST_UPDATED fix the plan's Risk table prescribed and the pair already applied at EMPTY_FILTER; no asserted behaviour changes.
